steps.title: Linked devices on WhatsApp
steps.expected: Only devices you recognise, each with a recent 'last active'.
steps.dangerSign: A device, computer or web session you don't recognise — someone else is reading your chats.
steps.fix: Tap the unknown device and Log out. Then turn on the security-code change alerts below.

steps.title: Two-step PIN on WhatsApp
steps.expected: Two-step verification is On and you know the PIN.
steps.dangerSign: It's Off, or a PIN you didn't set is on — someone could re-register your number.
steps.fix: Turn it on and set a PIN only you know. Add your email so you can reset it.

steps.title: Active sessions on Telegram
steps.expected: Only your own phones and computers.
steps.dangerSign: An unknown session, especially from another city or country.
steps.fix: Tap it and Terminate. Use 'Terminate all other sessions' if unsure, then set a 2-step password.

steps.title: Two-step password on Telegram
steps.where: Telegram → Settings → Privacy and Security → Two-Step Verification
steps.dangerSign: No password set — your account relies on the SMS code alone.
steps.fix: Set a Two-Step Verification password and a recovery email.

steps.title: Devices signed into your Google account
steps.expected: Only devices you own and still use.
steps.dangerSign: A device or session you don't recognise.
steps.fix: Open it and Sign out, then change your Google password.

steps.title: 2-Step Verification on Google
steps.expected: It's On, using your own phone or an authenticator / passkey.
steps.dangerSign: It's Off, or a phone number / authenticator you don't recognise is listed.
steps.fix: Turn it on with your own device and remove any second factor you don't recognise.

steps.title: Recovery email and phone on Google
steps.where: myaccount.google.com → Security → Recovery email / Recovery phone
steps.expected: Your own email and phone number.
steps.dangerSign: A recovery email or phone you don't recognise — an attacker can reset your password to it.
steps.fix: Replace it with your own, then sign out all other devices and change your password.

steps.title: Third-party access to your Google account
steps.where: myaccount.google.com → Security → Your connections to third-party apps
steps.expected: Only apps you chose and still use.
steps.dangerSign: An app with access to Gmail, Drive or your location that you don't recognise.

steps.title: Hidden forwarding and filters in Gmail
steps.where: Gmail (web) → Settings → Forwarding and POP/IMAP, and → Filters and Blocked Addresses
steps.expected: No forwarding address, and no filter that forwards or deletes your mail.
steps.dangerSign: Mail forwarded to an address you don't know, or a filter that hides bank/security mail.
steps.fix: Remove the forwarding address and delete the filter, then change your password.

steps.title: Devices on your Apple ID
steps.where: Settings → [your name] (Apple ID) → scroll to the device list
steps.dangerSign: A device you don't recognise can see your iCloud data and location.
steps.fix: Tap it → Remove from account, then change your Apple ID password.

steps.title: Two-factor and trusted numbers on Apple ID
steps.where: Settings → [your name] → Sign-In & Security → Two-Factor Authentication
steps.expected: On, with only your own trusted phone numbers.
steps.dangerSign: A trusted phone number you don't recognise.
steps.fix: Remove the unknown number and keep two-factor on.

steps.title: Who you share location with (Apple)
steps.where: Find My app → People, and Settings → [your name] → Find My → Share My Location
steps.expected: Only people you chose to share with.
steps.dangerSign: Your location is shared with someone you didn't intend, or didn't know about.
steps.fix: Stop sharing with that person. Check Settings → Privacy & Security → Location Services too.

steps.title: Where you're logged in (Facebook)
steps.where: Facebook → Settings → Password and security → Where you're logged in
steps.expected: Only your own devices and locations.
steps.dangerSign: A session in a place or on a device that isn't yours.
steps.fix: Log it out, turn on login alerts, and change your password.

steps.title: Login activity on Instagram
steps.where: Instagram → Settings → Accounts Center → Password and security → Where you're logged in
steps.fix: Log it out and change your password.

steps.title: Recent sign-in activity (Microsoft)
steps.dangerSign: A successful sign-in from a place or device that isn't yours.
steps.fix: Select 'This wasn't me', change your password, and review recovery info.

steps.title: Forwarding and rules in Outlook mail
steps.where: Outlook.com → Settings → Mail → Forwarding, and → Rules
steps.expected: No forwarding, and no rule that moves or deletes incoming mail.
steps.dangerSign: Forwarding to an unknown address, or a rule hiding security mail.
steps.fix: Turn off forwarding and delete the rule, then change your password.
